text: The same idea runs in your skin. Stem cells in the base layer of the outer skin keep dividing by mitosis. Daughter cells that move upwards differentiate: they flatten, specialise, and are eventually lost from the surface, while the base layer carries on. After a graze, extra divisions there, help replace the lost cells: that is tissue repair. Notice the two separate steps. Mitosis makes new cells, genetically identical to the stem cell. Differentiation makes them specialised.
